purpose: The two gaps this project had no answer for: a whole-system cross-check against a LICENSED transient code, and REAL operator field data with a known outcome. One open document carries both.
source: Roberts, T. (2019), 'Oil and Gas Field Application of Hydrate Kinetics Modeling', MEng thesis, Faculty of Engineering and Applied Science, Memorial University of Newfoundland, 55 pages. Read from the Memorial open repository (memorial.scholaris.ca/bitstreams/c53d348a-3091-4050-ba2c-50cdc0750741/download); the older research.library.mun.ca/13811/1/thesis.pdf now 301-redirects there. Numbers below are read from the thesis tables and figures directly.
what_it_is: OLGA -- the transient multiphase simulator this project has never been compared against -- coupled with CSMHyK, the Colorado School of Mines hydrate kinetics module, and applied to two real cases on an offshore development.

field_cases.outcome: A REAL HYDRATE BLOCKAGE, confirmed and remediated.
field_cases.evidence: The rigid spool sits open to flowline pressure, about 5,300 kPa measured at other production trees. Pressure built within the spool toward 8,000 kPa, which is what confirmed a blockage was present. Cleared safely by depressurisation.
field_cases.model_result: The coupled model correctly predicted the most likely LOCATION of the blockage, by volume percent of formed hydrate.
field_cases.author_caveat: The subcooling assumption 'may have been conservative'. Worth reading beside this project's own subcooling exponent. That used to be growth_exp_n = 1.0 -- an assumption chosen at the favourable end, and BELOW the published 1.5-2.5 range -- which made it the same class of concern from the opposite direction. The default is now 1.5 (Mori 2001, dT^3/2), inside the published range, so the two assumptions now err the same way rather than against each other.

field_cases.outcome: HYDRATE RISK CONDITIONS, NO BLOCKAGE -- a confirmed negative, and the harder test.
field_cases.what_happened: An emergency shutdown at 00:40. Flowlines left stagnant 11 h, taking the system 5 h beyond its 6 h no-touch time. Subsea pressure fell 4,800 -> 4,200 kPa on settle-out and cool-down. Blowdown at 11:40 took it to ~1,800 kPa. Hot-oil circulation started 16:20 (15.5 h dead) and finished 19:30. No blockage; production restarted without incident.
field_cases.segment_at_risk: Segments 1a and 1b, DC1 to the FPSO through the risers. Every other flowline showed no hydrate risk -- warmer fluids and more insulation. The thesis analyses 1a.

geometry_segment_1a.description: Figure 19 flowpath: a short dip below datum over the first ~60 m, up to about +8 m by ~90 m, then flat along the seabed to ~2,020 m, then the flexible riser -- up to ~70 m, back down to ~32 m, then to ~150 m at the FPSO. The mid-riser dip is a lazy-wave shape.
geometry_segment_1a.elevation_read_from: Figure 19, digitised by eye from the rendered page. Approximate; the thesis itself labels the layout distances 'approximate'.
geometry_segment_1a.wall_flowline: Table 7, 10 inch original flexible: carcass 6.0 mm, pressure sheath Gammaflex 7.0, zeta wire 10.0, armour 5.0 + 5.0, fabric tape 1.45, intermediate sheath 8.70, insulation MO1 11.0 (k = 0.0605), fabric tape 1.05, external sheath 11.40.
geometry_segment_1a.wall_riser: Table 6, 10 inch flexible riser -- carries NO insulation layer at all, so the last ~180 m cools faster than the flowline. RESOLVED: the solver now accepts an axially SEGMENTED wall (pipe.wall_layers as {from_m, to_m, layers} entries), so segment 1a is run as it is -- insulated flowline to 2020 m, bare riser beyond. Measured effect: U = 3.82 W/m2K on the flowline against 7.71 on the riser, so the riser loses heat twice as fast. Two single-stack arms remain as BOUNDS. Across those bounds the plug/no-plug bit and the max subcooling are unchanged, but the peak deposit moves by a factor of 2.43 (17.89 -> 43.56 mm) -- so the simplification does NOT decide the bit, and it DOES decide the magnitude, which is one of the three things scored against the reference.

field_cases.ambient: seawater -1.8 C, sea-floor current 0.94 m/s (thesis p. 23, same as case 1)
field_cases.model_result_quantitative: This is the part that makes case 2 scorable rather than a bare bit. OLGA + CSMHyK predicted hydrate first at the drill-centre manifold and at the base of the riser. At 11 h -- the real stagnant duration -- volume fractions were BELOW 2 % at the manifold and BELOW 1 % at the riser base. Growth accelerated markedly only from about 17 h. The thesis extended the run to 20 h purely as a sensitivity; the line was never stagnant that long.
field_cases.modelling_caveats_stated_by_the_author: A default subcooling onset of 3.6 C was used and the author calls it possibly conservative. Hydrate curves were built on lift gas with PURE water, no salt, which is conservative by a couple of degrees. The system is oil-dominated.
field_cases.why_it_matters: A validated negative is rarer than a validated positive and is the harder test: a model that predicts plugging everywhere passes case 1 and fails case 2. It also carries a quantitative reference -- <2 % and <1 % hydrate at 11 h -- so a solver can be scored on the MAGNITUDE it predicts, not only on whether it says plug or no plug.

field_crude_assay.why_this_matters_here: This project's fluid-identity gap was closed by RE-CUTTING the composition to satisfy density and phase behaviour -- a defensible regression, but a fluid with no field provenance. This is a published FIELD assay with lab PVT behind it, and its stock-tank density (883 kg/m3) is close to this case's 858, so it is a real alternative to a fitted cut.
field_crude_assay.note: C1 48.83 mol% against this project's re-cut 60.0. The assay is a genuinely different fluid on a different development, so it is a REFERENCE to characterise against, not a drop-in replacement for this case's composition.

limits: No dP, arrival-temperature or holdup TIME SERIES is tabulated for either case, so neither gives this solver a point-by-point profile to score itself against. What case 1 gives is a bit plus a location: a real blockage and a pressure build to 8,000 kPa. What case 2 gives is more -- a confirmed NEGATIVE with a quantitative model reference (<2 % and <1 % hydrate volume at 11 h, acceleration only from ~17 h), so magnitude can be checked and not only direction. Both are a different development, fluid and geometry from this project's case study, and the riser wall of case 2 (uninsulated, Table 6) is not representable in this solver's single wall stack.
status: SCORED. case/scripts/run_field_arm.py runs this solver on both cases -- arm 'asfound' (case 1, the spool that blocked), arm 'inhibited' (a control on the same spool with the methanol treatment that was skipped -- a counterfactual, NOT an observation) and arm 'case2' (the flowline that did not block). case/scripts/score_plugging_on_real_data.py collects the arms and reports the score with its interval. Earlier revisions of this file said 'nothing in this repository is scored against it yet'; that is no longer true.
